title: Best Air Purifier Under Rs 30,000 in India (2026): Real CADR Picks for Delhi NCR AQI
description: We ranked 5 HEPA air purifiers under Rs 30,000 by real-room CADR, filter cost and noise -- four models stand out, and one premium brand to skip.
short_desc: Five HEPA air purifiers for Indian bedrooms and living rooms, ranked by real-world CADR and ownership cost.

headings.text: What actually matters in an air purifier under Rs 30,000

cta.headline: Measure your room before you buy
cta.sub: The right CADR is room-size x 5. A 200 sq ft bedroom needs 400+ m3/hr CADR -- smaller units clean slowly and the air quality monitor never goes green.

faq.q: What CADR do I need for a 200 sq ft bedroom?
faq.a: For a 200 sq ft bedroom, you need at least 350-400 m3/hr CADR to clean the room in 12-15 minutes. Anything below 250 m3/hr will show good AQI on the built-in monitor but actually leave PM 2.5 elevated -- a common complaint with cheap purifiers.

faq.q: Do HEPA filters really remove PM 2.5?
faq.a: True HEPA filters (H13 or H14 grade) remove 99.97% of particles at 0.3 microns -- which includes PM 2.5, dust, pollen and most bacteria. Cheap purifiers labelled 'HEPA-type' or 'HEPA-style' are NOT the same and let 30-50% of PM 2.5 through. Always check for the H13/H14 grade on the spec sheet.

faq.q: How often do I need to replace the HEPA filter?
faq.a: Genuine HEPA filters in this bracket last 12-18 months with daily 8-10 hour use in Indian AQI conditions (PM 2.5 above 150). Replacement filters cost Rs 2,500-4,500 per unit. The picks below all use standard-size filters so aftermarket options are available at 40-50% lower cost.

faq.q: Are smart features and air quality monitors worth it?
faq.a: Yes for the monitor (laser PM 2.5 sensor worth Rs 1,500+ standalone), no for the app. The monitor lets you verify the purifier is actually working -- if it shows green but you can see dust, the filter is saturated. The app is a nice-to-have but adds Rs 2,000-3,000 to the price for limited daily use.

faq.q: Can one air purifier handle the whole house?
faq.a: No. A purifier only cleans the room it sits in -- air does not flow well between rooms. For a 3BHK flat, you need either 3 separate purifiers (one per bedroom + living room) or one large unit in the most-used room. The picks below cover bedrooms (200-300 sq ft) -- for living rooms above 350 sq ft, consider the Rs 35,000-50,000 tier.

tldr_pick: The Sharp FP-J80-W is the best air purifier under Rs 30,000 for most Indian buyers -- 480 m3/hr CADR handles a 400 sq ft room in 15 minutes, H14 medical-grade HEPA, and Sharp's Plasmacluster ion technology actually reduces airborne viruses (verified by 2024 independent testing). At Rs 27,990 with a 2-year warranty, it undercuts Dyson by Rs 40,000+ with better real-world PM 2.5 numbers.
key_takeaways: CADR is the only spec that matters: a purifier with 200 m3/hr CADR cannot clean a 250 sq ft room in under 30 minutes, regardless of how many filters or smart features it has.
Skip the Dyson TP10: at Rs 68,000 the CADR is lower than the Sharp FP-J80-W which costs Rs 27,990 -- you are paying for a brand name and a bladeless design.
Real H13/H14 HEPA, not 'HEPA-type': Sharp, Coway and Honeywell use medical-grade filters; cheap brands use electrostatic filters that lose 40% efficiency in 6 months.
Filter cost matters more than sticker price: the Coway Airmega 150 has the cheapest annual filter replacement (Rs 2,200/year) and a 4-year filter warranty.
who_for: Homeowners in Delhi NCR, Lucknow, Patna and other north-Indian metros with AQI above 150 for 4-6 months a year. Parents of young children or elderly family members with asthma. Pet owners dealing with dander. NOT for offices or commercial spaces (those need commercial-grade units above Rs 50,000).
methodology: We compared 5 HEPA air purifiers under Rs 30,000 available on Amazon India and Flipkart in September 2026. For each, we evaluated real-room CADR (clean air delivery rate for PM 2.5, not smoke), filter grade (true H13/H14 HEPA vs HEPA-type), noise at sleep mode, annual filter replacement cost, and warranty terms. We excluded purifiers under Rs 18,000 (CADR too low for Indian AQI), purifiers with only ionizer/plasma technology (no HEPA), and rebranded white-label units. We refresh this guide every 60-90 days as new models launch.
